name: Відхід і захист
description:
You already know how to defend one attacked piece. But what can you do to defend against a double attack? That is not so easy. But it is not impossible, either.

Sometimes you can solve two problems in one move. You have to combine two defensive technics to do that. This lesson covers moving away plus protecting.

Take a look at example 1. White faces a double attack on his king and rook. Still, he is able to save himself!

In example 2, White wriggles out of a skewer by means of moving away plus protecting.

Even when two pieces are attacked at once, you may be able to save them by moving away plus protecting. See example 3.

In example 4, too, White has two problems. Yet, he can save his rook and prevent mate. By moving away plus protection. Nice job!

What do you have to do?
Defend against a double attack. Use moving away plus protecting. Remember to do this safely.

examples.text:
A double attack on White’s king (check) and rook.
White can get out of check in many ways.
But the best move is to push his king towards the rook.
The king now defends the rook. White does not lose points.

Here we have a skewer.
Click on the play button to see where the king moves to.
He moves out of check.
On his new spot he can defend the rook.
Nothing lost for White.

Black’s queen attacks both the rook and the knight.
But White’s rook can move away to a square from which it can protect the knight.
Click on the play button to watch the moves.

Would it also be okay for the white knight to follow the red arrow?
No, it wouldn’t. The knight would protect the rook, but it would be unguarded itself.
Black would take the knight.

The queen attacks the rook and a mating square.
But White can save his rook and prevent mate.
How? By moving the rook to the first row.
From there it protects the mating square.

texts: Try to solve two problems at once.
